answer: Each identity claims one karst spring outlet in the registry, one per identity, and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it buys one umber dose coded to that outlet and files a sonnet log of 14 hourly readings. Any auditor recomputes the decay curve from dose and sensor times; a missing line, reused dose code, or mismatched curve burns the bond. The k-th outlet pays 60+20(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 10,050,000 in fees plus 80,000 in bonds. A rented tracer ring fails: one dose cannot yield two matching curves. An honest operator pays 60 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
